idiom_name: hand-written Enricher + abstract DataSource + unordered_map cache
implementation_notes: No C++ library implements the Content Enricher, so the realization is a hand-written enricher over an abstract DataSource (virtual find(key) returning std::optional<Record>), with a std::unordered_map in front of the source to absorb repeated keys. Keeping the source abstract lets tests inject a stub and production inject the SQL or HTTP client; the merge is a plain copy of the resolved fields into the message type. Choose this shape whenever the resource call is synchronous and the flow already owns a thread for the message.
pitfalls: Copying a reference or pointer into the datasource's internal cache makes the enriched message dangle when the cache evicts; copy the values, not the addresses.
A virtual call per field looks tidy but degenerates into an N+1 of lookups; resolve once per message key and merge afterwards.
An unbounded unordered_map cache turns the enricher into a memory leak with a lookup API; bound it or expire entries.

variants.name: Asio coroutine awaiting the resource lookup (C++20)
variants.idiom_name: co_await the resource call inside a Boost.Asio awaitable
variants.implementation_notes: With C++20 stackless coroutines and Boost.Asio the enrichment step stops blocking: the resource call is awaited (co_await src.async_find(id)) and the coroutine resumes on the io_context when the data arrives, so one thread keeps enriching messages while lookups are in flight. The DataSource interface stays, but its operations return awaitables and the per-message work is co_spawned. Prefer it when the resource is a network service and the flow must not pin a thread per message.
pitfalls: The coroutine must own the message and datasource state across suspension points; references into the caller's frame dangle on resume.
Detached co_spawn swallows failures - attach a completion handler or an exception channel, or a failed lookup disappears silently.
A blocking datasource call inside the coroutine stalls the whole io_context, which is exactly what the coroutine form was meant to avoid.
